prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE finished desktop product interface image for MetroNest, a property maintenance operations tool. This is an interface redesign concept with sample data, not a live client screenshot. A completely distinct client identity: ink-blue #142d3e, deep teal #087c78, warm white #f5f5f0, steel rules. No lilac, purple, black sidebar or portfolio branding. Architectural, precise and dependable, dense enough for a real property operations team. Sharp readable typography. Flat front-facing interface fills the entire 1600x1000 landscape image; no device frame, shadows around screenshot, surrounding whitespace or perspective.
Use horizontal navigation across the top: a refined typographic “MetroNest” wordmark with small geometric MN mark, then “Requests”, “Contractors”, “Settings”; at right a visible “Sample data” label. Deep ink-blue header, teal active underline. White main workspace, no vertical sidebar. Main title “Maintenance requests”. A compact filter toolbar: “All 4”, “Urgent 1”, “Ready 1”, “Waiting 2” and search.
Upper half is a professional full-width data table with columns “Request”, “Property”, “Status”, “Priority”. Four readable rows: “Plumbing request” / “Unit 8 · King Street” / “Ready” / “High”; “Heating inspection” / “Unit 3 · Park Road” / “Waiting” / “Medium”; “Faulty extractor” / “Unit 12 · Station View” / “Waiting” / “Low”; “Door repair” / “Unit 5 · Victoria Court” / “Open” / “Medium”. First row selected with soft blue-green fill, no side accent stripe. Restrained amber high-priority indicators. Avoid stat cards, decorative charts, giant totals, pills everywhere.
Lower half is one continuous selected-request inspection panel with aligned three columns, thin dividers, editorial hierarchy. Header “Plumbing request” and small “MN-DE4280 · WEB CHAT”. First column: heading “Triage summary”; copy “Potential damage or service disruption. Confirm tenant access before dispatch.”; address “Unit 8, 14 King Street” / “Manchester M1 6EU”. Second column: heading “Rough price band”; prominent but appropriately sized “£260–£700”; note “Indicative only. Contractor quote takes precedence.”; “Approval limit £650”; a visible off switch labelled “Auto-approval off”. Third column: heading “Recommended contractor”; “RapidPipe Plumbing”; “Plumbing · Same-day contact”; heading “Next step”; “Approve contractor contact and confirm tenant access.” A single dark teal action “Approve contractor” and understated secondary “Request more details”. Final discreet note “Requests over £650 need approval.”
Precise alignment, compact useful density, excellent readable text, full image edges all content visible. This should look like bespoke operational software built for this property brand, structurally different from a trades quote editor. All data illustrative; keep Sample data visible.
intent: MetroNest interface redesign concept with sample data; no underlying application changes
processing: Converted generated PNG to WebP at quality 94, native dimensions retained
